q: In Indian Railways, the satellite and GPS based system 'RTIS', provided on locomotives for automatic tracking of trains, stands for:
e: RTIS stands for Real Time Train Information System, the satellite and GPS based system fitted on locomotives that automatically reports train location and movement in real time.

q: In railway pension administration, the portal 'ARPAN', through which pension sanction and e-PPO generation are processed, stands for:

options.D: All India Railway Pension Access Network

e: ARPAN is the Advanced Railway Pension Access Network, the Railways e-governance system that automates pension sanction and sends e-PPOs digitally to banks for payment.

q: In the family of railway organisations, 'IRFC' stands for:
e: IRFC is the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, the dedicated financing arm of Indian Railways that raises funds from the market for rolling stock and other railway assets.

q: In the family of railway organisations, 'IPRCL' stands for:

options.B: Indian Port Rail and Ropeway Corporation Limited
options.C: Indian Ports and Rail Corporation Limited

e: IPRCL is the Indian Port Rail and Ropeway Corporation Limited, the company that builds last-mile rail and ropeway connectivity to ports and other sites.

q: In the context of the regional rapid transit system of the National Capital Region, 'NCRTC' stands for:
e: NCRTC is the National Capital Region Transport Corporation, the joint venture implementing the regional rapid transit system (RRTS) in the National Capital Region.

q: The 'SwaRail' SuperApp of Indian Railways, released for beta testing on 31 January 2025 as a one-stop platform for ticketing, enquiries and RailMadad, was developed and released by:
e: The SwaRail SuperApp, released for beta testing on 31 January 2025 as a single platform for ticketing, enquiries and RailMadad, was developed by CRIS, the Railways own IT organisation.

q: 'Rudrastra', the longest freight train of Indian Railways whose trial run was conducted in August 2025 between Ganjkhwaja and Garhwa Road, was formed by coupling six BOXN rakes comprising a total of:
e: Rudrastra was formed by coupling six BOXN rakes; at 59 wagons per rake this gives 354 wagons, making it the longest freight train run by Indian Railways.

q: The first cherry parcel train of Jammu and Kashmir, which left Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra in May-June 2025 carrying about 24 tonnes of cherries, was run to which station in Mumbai?
e: The first cherry parcel train from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra carried about 24 tonnes of Jammu and Kashmir cherries to Bandra Terminus in Mumbai.

q: The railway station in Maharashtra which was officially renamed as 'Ahilyanagar' in September 2025, in honour of Lokmata Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar, was earlier known as:
e: Ahmednagar station in Maharashtra was renamed Ahilyanagar in September 2025 to honour Lokmata Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar, after whom the new name is formed.

q: The 21 km long tunnel of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor, a part of which passes under the Thane Creek, is being built between:
e: The 21 km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail tunnel, part of which passes under Thane Creek, is being built between Bandra Kurla Complex and Shilphata.

q: The 'e-RCT' system, introduced as part of the complete digitisation of the Railway Claims Tribunal, mainly enables claimants to:

options.A: Book reserved tickets without a service charge
options.B: Track the running status of trains in real time
options.C: Claim refund of freight charges at stations
options.D: File claims online from any location and follow their cases electronically

e: e-RCT digitises the Railway Claims Tribunal, enabling claimants to file claims online from any location and follow their cases electronically instead of visiting the tribunal.

q: India's first 9,000 HP electric freight locomotive, dedicated to the nation at Dahod in May 2025, has been christened:
e: India's first 9,000 HP electric freight locomotive, dedicated at Dahod in May 2025, is christened D-9, the name given to this locomotive class built there.

q: The first section of the Kolkata Metro's Yellow Line, opened in August 2025, connects Noapara with which station serving the airport?
e: The first section of the Kolkata Metro Yellow Line, opened in August 2025, runs from Noapara to Jai Hind (Bimanbandar), the station serving the airport.

q: The New Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge inaugurated in April 2025, has a length of about:
e: The New Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge inaugurated in April 2025, is about 2.08 km long across the Palk Strait.

q: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, the world's highest railway arch bridge dedicated to the nation in June 2025, has a total length of about:
e: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, the world's highest railway arch bridge, has a total length of about 1,315 metres.

q: The 'Natyashastra', the celebrated Sanskrit treatise on theatre, dance and music, is traditionally attributed to:
e: The Natyashastra, the foundational Sanskrit treatise on theatre, dance and music, is traditionally attributed to the sage Bharata Muni.

q: The Tamil epic 'Kamba Ramayanam', the celebrated Tamil version of the Ramayana, was composed by:
e: Kamba Ramayanam, the celebrated Tamil version of the Ramayana, was composed by the Tamil poet Kambar.

q: The Hindi epic poem 'Kamayani' (1936), centred on the mythological flood survivor Manu, was written by:
e: Kamayani (1936), the Hindi epic poem centred on Manu, the survivor of the great flood, was written by Jaishankar Prasad, a leading figure of Chhayavad poetry.

q: The Punjabi novel 'Pinjar' (The Skeleton), centred on the abducted girl Puro during the Partition, was written by:
e: Pinjar (The Skeleton), the Punjabi novel about Puro, abducted during the Partition, was written by Amrita Pritam.

q: The Marathi novel 'Mrityunjay' (The Death Conqueror), a celebrated retelling of the life of Karna, was written by:
e: Mrityunjay, the celebrated Marathi retelling of the life of Karna from the Mahabharata, was written by Shivaji Sawant.

q: The Marathi novel 'Yayati' (1959), based on the Mahabharata king Yayati and winner of the Jnanpith Award, was written by:
e: Yayati (1959), Vishnu Sakharam Khandekar's Marathi novel on the Mahabharata king Yayati, won him the Jnanpith Award.

q: The 'Gulistan' (The Rose Garden), the famous Persian book of prose and verse stories and moral sayings, was written by:
e: The Gulistan (The Rose Garden), the famous Persian book of stories and moral sayings in prose and verse, was written by the poet Saadi of Shiraz.

q: The 'Tao Te Ching', the foundational text of Taoism, is traditionally attributed to the Chinese sage:
e: The Tao Te Ching, the foundational text of Taoism, is traditionally attributed to the Chinese sage Laozi.

q: The book 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money' (1936), a landmark work of modern economics, was written by:
e: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936) was written by John Maynard Keynes and founded modern macroeconomics.

q: The book 'On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres' (1543), which presented the heliocentric model of the universe, was written by:
e: On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres (1543) was written by Nicolaus Copernicus and presented the heliocentric model, with the Sun at the centre.

q: The book 'Silent Spring' (1962), which drew attention to the dangers of pesticides such as DDT to the environment, was written by:
e: Silent Spring (1962), which exposed the dangers of pesticides such as DDT to the environment, was written by Rachel Carson.

q: The play 'Pygmalion', in which Professor Higgins transforms the flower girl Eliza Doolittle, was written by:
e: Pygmalion, in which Professor Higgins transforms flower girl Eliza Doolittle, was written by George Bernard Shaw.

q: The play 'Death of a Salesman' (1949), centred on the ageing travelling salesman Willy Loman, was written by:
e: Death of a Salesman (1949), centred on the ageing travelling salesman Willy Loman, was written by the American playwright Arthur Miller.

q: The novel 'The Stranger' (1942), centred on Meursault, who shoots a man on a beach in Algiers, was written by:
e: The Stranger (1942), centred on Meursault, who shoots a man on a beach in Algiers, was written by Albert Camus.

q: The novel 'Beloved' (1987), centred on the former slave Sethe and the memory of her dead daughter, was written by:
e: Beloved (1987), centred on the former slave Sethe and the memory of her dead daughter, was written by Toni Morrison.

q: The novel 'Life of Pi' (2001), in which the boy Pi Patel survives on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger, was written by:
e: Life of Pi (2001), in which Pi Patel survives on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger, was written by Yann Martel.

q: The Mudaliar Commission (1952-53), appointed by the Government of India, was set up to inquire into and report on:
e: The Mudaliar Commission (1952-53), headed by Dr A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar, was appointed to inquire into secondary education in India.

q: The Lyngdoh Committee (2006), headed by former Chief Election Commissioner J. M. Lyngdoh, is associated with guidelines on:

options.A: Elections to student unions in universities

e: The Lyngdoh Committee (2006), headed by former Chief Election Commissioner J. M. Lyngdoh, laid down guidelines for elections to student unions in universities.

q: The Police Act Drafting Committee (2005), which prepared the draft Model Police Act, was chaired by:
e: The Police Act Drafting Committee (2005), which prepared the draft Model Police Act, was chaired by the jurist Soli Sorabjee.

q: The Karve Committee (1955) is associated with recommendations on the development of:
e: The Karve Committee (1955) made recommendations on the development of village and small-scale industries in India.

q: The Shunglu Committee (2010), headed by former Comptroller and Auditor General V. K. Shunglu, was set up to inquire into irregularities in the:

options.C: Organisation and conduct of the Commonwealth Games at Delhi

e: The Shunglu Committee (2010), headed by former CAG V. K. Shunglu, inquired into irregularities in the organisation and conduct of the Delhi Commonwealth Games.

q: The Bhuria Committee (1995), whose recommendations led to the PESA Act of 1996, dealt with the extension of provisions relating to ____ to the Scheduled Areas:
e: The Bhuria Committee (1995) dealt with extending the provisions relating to Panchayats to the Scheduled Areas, leading to the PESA Act of 1996.

q: The Tax Administration Reform Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Tax Administration Reform Commission, set up to reform India's tax administration, was chaired by Parthasarathi Shome.

q: The Easwar Committee (2015) was set up by the Government of India for the:

options.A: Review of the fiscal responsibility framework
options.B: Simplification of the provisions of income-tax law
options.D: Restructuring of the Food Corporation of India

e: The Easwar Committee (2015) was set up for the simplification of the provisions of income-tax law, under Justice R. V. Easwar.

q: The Fifth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Fifth Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1968, was chaired by Mahavir Tyagi.

q: The Fifth Central Pay Commission, constituted in 1994, was chaired by:
e: The Fifth Central Pay Commission, constituted in 1994, was chaired by Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian.

q: The Abhijit Sen Committee (2007) was set up by the Government of India to study the impact of:

options.A: Foreign direct investment in retail trade

e: The Abhijit Sen Committee (2007) studied the impact of futures trading in agricultural commodities on prices and farmers.

q: The Investment Commission, set up by the Government of India in 2004 to attract foreign and domestic investment, was headed by:
e: The Investment Commission, set up in 2004 to attract foreign and domestic investment into India, was headed by Ratan Tata.

q: The 'Zloty' is the currency of:
e: The Zloty is the currency of Poland; Hungary uses the Forint and Romania the Leu.

q: The 'Naira' is the currency of:
e: The Naira is the currency of Nigeria; Kenya uses the Shilling and Ghana the Cedi.

q: The headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the UN aviation agency, is located at Montreal in Canada.

q: The headquarters of Interpol, the International Criminal Police Organization, is located at:
e: Interpol, the International Criminal Police Organization, has its headquarters at Lyon in France.

q: The headquarters of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is located at:
e: The headquarters of OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, is located at Vienna in Austria.

q: The largest peninsula in the world is the:
e: The Arabian Peninsula is the largest peninsula in the world, larger than the Indian, Iberian and Scandinavian peninsulas.

q: The National Aquatic Animal of India, declared in 2009, is the:
e: The Gangetic river dolphin was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009, in recognition of this endangered river species.

q: The longest National Highway of India, running from Srinagar to Kanyakumari, is:
e: NH 44, running from Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south, is the longest National Highway of India.

q: India's longest sea bridge, the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link inaugurated in January 2024, has been named:
e: The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, India's longest sea bridge inaugurated in January 2024, has been named Atal Setu, after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

q: 'Blue vitriol', a blue crystalline substance long used as a fungicide, is chemically:
e: Blue vitriol is the common name of copper sulphate, a blue crystalline salt long used as a fungicide.

q: The scientific study of fossils is known as:
e: Palaeontology is the scientific study of fossils, the preserved remains and traces of ancient life.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Botany'?
e: Theophrastus, the Greek philosopher who wrote foundational works on plants, is regarded as the Father of Botany.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Medicine'?
e: Hippocrates, the Greek physician associated with the Hippocratic Oath, is regarded as the Father of Medicine.

q: World Book and Copyright Day, proclaimed by UNESCO, is celebrated every year on:
e: UNESCO proclaimed World Book and Copyright Day, celebrated every year on 23 April, the date linked to the deaths of Shakespeare and Cervantes.

q: Ashgabat is the capital of:
e: Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan, one of the Central Asian republics.

q: Bishkek is the capital of:
e: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan, the Central Asian republic whose other neighbours include Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

q: The 'Birr' is the currency of:
e: The Birr is the currency of Ethiopia; Eritrea uses the Nakfa and Somalia the Shilling.

q: The Railway Board was set up in 1905 on the recommendations of which committee?
e: The Railway Board was set up in 1905 on the recommendations of the Robertson Committee, which had examined railway administration and finance.

q: The regrouping of the Indian Railways into zonal railways was recommended by which committee?
e: The regrouping of Indian Railways into zonal railways was recommended by the Kunzru Committee, after which the zonal system was formed in the early 1950s.

q: The Expert Committee on Modernisation of Indian Railways, which submitted its report in 2012, was chaired by:
e: The Expert Committee on Modernisation of Indian Railways, which reported in 2012, was chaired by Sam Pitroda.

q: Who became the first woman Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board in 2023?
e: Jaya Varma Sinha became the first woman Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board in 2023.

q: In the restructuring of the Railway Board, the post of Chairman, Railway Board was redesignated as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer in the year:
e: In the 2020 restructuring of the Railway Board, the post of Chairman, Railway Board was redesignated as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.

q: 'Bholu', the official mascot of Indian Railways, is a:

options.A: Tiger dressed as a station master
options.C: Lion dressed as a loco pilot
options.D: Horse dressed as a ticket examiner

e: Bholu, the official mascot of Indian Railways, is an elephant dressed as a guard, holding a signal lamp.

q: The Railway Protection Force was constituted under the Railway Protection Force Act passed in the year:
e: The Railway Protection Force was constituted under the Railway Protection Force Act passed in 1957.

q: The first Railway Budget of independent India, presented in November 1947, was presented by:
e: The first Railway Budget of independent India, presented in November 1947, was presented by John Mathai.

q: The Centralised Training Academy for Railway Accounts (CTARA), which trains the officers of the railway accounts service, is located at:
e: The Centralised Training Academy for Railway Accounts (CTARA), which trained railway accounts officers, is located at Secunderabad.

q: The Konkan Railway line, running from Roha to Thokur, passes through which set of States?
e: The Konkan Railway line from Roha to Thokur passes through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka along the west coast.

q: The Principal Bench of the Railway Claims Tribunal is located at:
e: The Principal Bench of the Railway Claims Tribunal is located at New Delhi, with other benches across the country.

q: A division of Indian Railways is headed by an officer designated as the:
e: A division of Indian Railways is headed by the Divisional Railway Manager, who works under the General Manager of the zone.

q: After the restructuring of the Railway Board in 2020, the finance function in the Board is headed by the:
e: After the 2020 restructuring of the Railway Board, the finance function is headed by the Member (Finance), replacing the earlier Financial Commissioner (Railways).

q: The first Chairman and Managing Director of the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited, who headed the construction of the Konkan Railway line, was:
e: E. Sreedharan was the first Chairman and Managing Director of Konkan Railway Corporation Limited and headed construction of the Konkan Railway line.

q: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Mysuru functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Mysuru functions under South Western Railway, the zone for most of Karnataka.

q: The Wagon Repair Shop at Raipur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Wagon Repair Shop at Raipur functions under South East Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Bilaspur.

q: The Mechanical Workshop at Samastipur, known for the manufacture and overhaul of wagons, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Mechanical Workshop at Samastipur, known for manufacture and overhaul of wagons, functions under East Central Railway.

q: The Railway Workshop at Dibrugarh in Assam functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Railway Workshop at Dibrugarh in Assam functions under Northeast Frontier Railway, the zone serving the North-East.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Jodhpur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Jodhpur functions under North Western Railway, whose headquarters is at Jaipur.

q: The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala is situated in the State of:
e: The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala is situated in Punjab, where it manufactures passenger coaches for Indian Railways.

q: The Modern Coach Factory at Lalganj, near Raebareli, is located in the State of:
e: The Modern Coach Factory at Lalganj, near Raebareli, is located in Uttar Pradesh.

q: India's first electric locomotive shed, set up in 1928, is located at:
e: India's first electric locomotive shed, set up in 1928, is located at Kalyan in Maharashtra.

q: The headquarters of the North Western Railway is located at:
e: The headquarters of North Western Railway is located at Jaipur in Rajasthan.

q: The headquarters of the South East Central Railway is located at:
e: The headquarters of South East Central Railway is located at Bilaspur in Chhattisgarh.

q: In Indian Railways, 'ART', deployed at nominated stations for restoration work after an accident, stands for:
e: ART stands for Accident Relief Train, deployed at nominated stations with equipment and staff for restoration work after an accident.

q: In Indian Railways, 'HOG', the system under which the power supply for the coaches of a train is drawn from the locomotive, stands for:
e: HOG stands for Head On Generation, the system under which power for train coaches is drawn from the locomotive instead of separate generator cars.

q: In Indian Railways, 'MEMU', the train services run on mainline sections with electric multiple unit stock, stands for:
e: MEMU stands for Mainline Electric Multiple Unit, the electric multiple unit services run on mainline sections of Indian Railways.

q: In railway operations, 'CTC', under which the movement of trains over a section is controlled from a central location, stands for:
e: CTC stands for Centralised Traffic Control, under which train movements over a section are controlled from one central location.

q: In Indian Railways, 'EOTT', the device fitted at the end of a freight train in place of a brake van for monitoring the train's completeness, stands for:
e: EOTT stands for End of Train Telemetry, the device fitted at the end of a freight train in place of a brake van to confirm the train is complete and intact.

q: In Indian Railways, 'NMG', the rakes of converted passenger coaches used mainly for carrying automobiles, stands for:
e: NMG stands for New Modified Goods, the rakes of converted passenger coaches used mainly for carrying automobiles.

q: In Indian Railways, 'WILD', the trackside equipment installed to detect defective wheels of passing trains, stands for:
e: WILD stands for Wheel Impact Load Detector, the trackside equipment that detects defective wheels on passing trains by measuring impact loads.

q: In railway track maintenance, 'USFD', the technique used for detecting internal defects in rails, stands for:
e: USFD stands for Ultrasonic Flaw Detection, the technique using ultrasonic waves to detect internal defects in rails.

q: In the electrical organisation of Indian Railways, 'TRD', which looks after the overhead equipment and power supply installations, stands for:
e: TRD stands for Traction Distribution, the electrical organisation looking after overhead equipment and traction power supply installations.

q: In a zonal railway headquarters, 'PCSO' stands for:
e: PCSO stands for Principal Chief Safety Officer, the principal head for safety in a zonal railway headquarters.

q: In a zonal railway headquarters, 'PCMD' stands for:
e: PCMD stands for Principal Chief Medical Director, the principal head of the medical department in a zonal railway headquarters.

q: Who took charge as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board in September 2024?
e: Satish Kumar took charge as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board in September 2024, succeeding Jaya Varma Sinha.

q: Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, the number of stations identified for redevelopment across Indian Railways is:
e: Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, 1,309 stations have been identified for redevelopment across Indian Railways.

q: The capital outlay provided for Indian Railways in the Union Budget for 2025-26 was:
e: The capital outlay provided for Indian Railways in the Union Budget 2025-26 was Rs 2.65 lakh crore.

q: The Lucknow-New Delhi Tejas Express, started in 2019 as the first train of Indian Railways to be run by a subsidiary of the Railways instead of the Railways itself, was operated by:

options.D: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: The Lucknow-New Delhi Tejas Express of 2019, the first train run by a Railways subsidiary instead of the Railways itself, was operated by IRCTC.

q: The total length of the Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, dedicated to the nation in June 2025, is about:
e: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, dedicated to the nation in June 2025, has a total length of about 1,315 metres.
